title: left-nav sections for the sports vertical
acceptance: VerticalNavLink in apps/web/src/verticals.ts supports optional section ('library' | 'discover' | 'tools') and disabled fields; the sports vertical declares: Dashboard (top-level, disabled), Library -> Athletes, Discover -> Teams, Games, Events (all disabled), Tools -> Shortlists, Compare (both disabled); music and creators navLinks are unchanged and flat

Layout.tsx renders localized section headers (LIBRARY, DISCOVER, TOOLS) above their grouped links; unsectioned links render above the first section without a header; a vertical with no sectioned links renders exactly as today
Disabled nav items do not navigate, carry aria-disabled, and are visually muted; enabled items keep the existing active/hover behavior
Every sports nav item renders a FontAwesome icon imported by individual path; no Unicode symbols
All new user-facing strings go through Lingui and are translated in all 7 locales in the common catalog; lingui compile --strict passes via the repo checks

Tests under apps/web/src/layout cover section grouping, disabled item non-navigation and aria-disabled, and flat rendering for verticals without sections; pnpm typecheck, pnpm test, and pnpm build pass
verification_cmd: pnpm --filter web exec vitest run src/layout
notes: PRD: docs/PRD.md '## Leagues list (sports vertical)' requirement 7. User-confirmed: full mock nav ships now with not-yet-built destinations disabled. The Leagues nav item itself lands in phase 05 with its route - do not add a link to /sports/leagues in this phase. Nav grouping is presentation in route/nav code, permitted by the access-and-feature-gating architecture; do not add feature availability or route inventories to the documented VerticalConfig contract. Disabled presentation detail (tooltip vs plain muted) is the writer's call within the design language.
review_findings:
SHOULD_FIX:
- apps/web/src/layout/components/VerticalNav.tsx:12 — SECTIONS is typed `readonly {id: VerticalNavSection; label}[]`, which does not force coverage of the union; adding a fourth section id (phase 05+) silently drops every link in it from the nav with no compile error — build it from a `Record<VerticalNavSection, MessageDescriptor>` plus an explicit order tuple so an omission is a type error
- apps/web/src/layout/components/VerticalNavItem.tsx:31-39 — `aria-disabled` is not a global ARIA state, and the disabled branch renders Mantine NavLink as an `<a>` with no href, which maps to role `generic` where ARIA attributes are unsupported; assistive tech announces plain text with no disabled state, so the criterion is met in the DOM only — add `role="link"` (or render `component="button"` with `disabled`) so the attribute is exposed; the test asserts the raw attribute and passes either way
- apps/web/src/layout/Layout.test.tsx:83 — `library.textContent` uses `toContain` while the sibling Discover/Tools assertions use `toBe`, so a stray link leaking into the Library group would not fail — use `toBe("LibraryAthletes")` for parity
- apps/web/src/layout/components/VerticalNavItem.tsx:28-29 — comment restates the code it sits above ("No Link means no href", "Mantine's `disabled` supplies the muting"), which comment-discipline forbids — delete it; the branch is self-evident from the absence of `component={Link}`
- apps/web/src/locales/common/ja/messages.po — "Discover" is translated 発見 (the noun "a discovery"), which reads oddly as a nav section header; 探索 (cf. the Korean 탐색 already used) fits the navigation context

BACKLOG_WORTHY:
- medium — verticals.ts navLinks now lists six paths with no corresponding route, duplicating the router's catalog; apps/web/AGENTS.md asks navigation visibility to be driven from route metadata — unify once the real routes land
- low — disabled nav items give no affordance explaining why they are inert (no tooltip/"Coming soon"), and Mantine's `opacity: 0.4` on white over teal.9 leaves them near the contrast floor
- low — VerticalNavItem calls useLocation() per item while Layout already holds the location; pass the active path down if nav item count grows
